context.exploration_scope: Executed PHASE-SSI-S10's connected trigger->Principle judgment path once: compared the real state PHASE-SSI-S10 last recorded against a fresh read of the same real files, gating any comparison/Outcome strictly on an actual detected change

problem: PHASE-SSI-S10 connected the trigger but reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER on its own first check -- the connection had not yet been exercised a second time to confirm the baseline genuinely advances between checks (i.e. this phase compares against S10s checkpoint, not S5s original snapshot) rather than silently re-comparing against a stale reference forever.

decision.decision_summary: No real state change detected relative to the PHASE-SSI-S10 checkpoint (chain_status, gpu_available, and hold_status all still match) -- correctly ended without performing any comparison or Outcome.

action.action_summary: Compared the real state PHASE-SSI-S10 last recorded against a fresh read of the real trace chain and PRODUCTION_VALIDATION_HOLD.json; gated all further comparison and Outcome strictly on an actual detected change; on change, computed the independent judgment before the Principle-guided judgment, compared them, and recorded an advisory-only Outcome; never wrote to the real chain/hold files.

result.note: Correctly reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER against the advanced S10 checkpoint -- confirms the trigger baseline moves forward each execution rather than staying pinned to a stale reference, which is the intended repeatable-trigger behavior.

cause.root_cause_summary: A trigger that always compares against the same original snapshot would eventually report a stale "change" the moment ANYTHING differs from that first baseline, even after several no-op checks already logged the same difference -- advancing the comparison baseline to the last actual checkpoint (S10, not S5) is what keeps repeated executions of this trigger meaningful rather than redundant.

lesson: A real trigger has to be executed more than once, with the baseline advancing to the previous execution's checkpoint each time, before "connected to the real flow" is actually demonstrated rather than merely asserted after a single check -- and an advisory Outcome, recorded but never written back to the real files it was computed from, is how a real trigger stays observably real without becoming an unreviewed automatic action.
